name: Raphael AI
tagline: Browser based text-to-image generator with an editor that also takes uploaded JPG or PNG files.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Free tier is described as personal and noncommercial with queues and watermarks, paid tiers differ.

verdictSummary: The product here is a thin, pleasant front end over open weight diffusion models, and front ends are exactly what coding agents are good at. An agent can give you a prompt box, a seed field, an image-to-image upload path and a side-by-side compare grid in one sitting, and the generations are yours with no watermark and no noncommercial clause. The catch is the part that is not code: you need either a GPU with enough VRAM to run a FLUX or SDXL class model, or an inference API key, which means you have swapped one hosted dependency for another. Quality parity is realistic because the underlying weights are public, but speed and the no-setup convenience are not free. Build it if you already have the hardware or you are comfortable paying per image instead of per month.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that generates images from a text prompt, re-rolls variations with changed lighting or background wording at a fixed or random seed, accepts uploaded JPG or PNG for image-to-image, and keeps everything in a local gallery you can compare two at a time.
requirements: A GPU with 12 GB or more VRAM for local generation, or an inference API key for hosted runs
Python 3.11 and about 25 GB of disk for model weights if running locally
Willingness to wait on a first run model download
whatYouLose: Zero setup: no weights to download, no CUDA versions to argue with, no cold starts
Someone else's queue and GPU fleet, so your 30 second generation does not become a 4 minute one
Whatever prompt enhancement, upscaling and preset pipelines the hosted editor layers on top of the raw model
Mobile access, since a local app only exists while your machine is on
Legal convenience: a paid tier that spells out commercial rights in writing, instead of you reading model licenses yourself
moatNotes: Inference hardware is the real asset, not the model. The open weights everyone builds on are a commodity; renting GPUs at scale is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because GPU time is the actual product and most people do not own a GPU. A hosted generator turns a 30 GB download, a driver stack and a 20 minute cold start into a text box that answers in seconds from a phone. Add a clear commercial license on the paid tier and you have something a freelancer can bill against without reading a model card. The code is cheap, the machine under it is not.
notes: The UI is a weekend's worth of work; the GPU bill is permanent.
prompt:
Build a local text-to-image studio as a single Python project in this empty folder. No accounts, no telemetry, no cloud database.

Stack, non negotiable:
- FastAPI backend, Uvicorn, Python 3.11
- Hugging Face diffusers for generation, torch with CUDA if available
- SQLite via sqlite3 for the gallery index, images written to ./outputs
- Frontend is server rendered Jinja2 templates plus vanilla JS and plain CSS. No React, no build step.

Model handling:
- Default pipeline is black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell for text-to-image, 4 steps, loaded lazily on first request and cached in memory.
- Image-to-image uses the FLUX img2img pipeline with a strength slider from 0.2 to 0.9.
- If env var USE_REMOTE is true, route generation to the Replicate HTTP API instead, reading REPLICATE_API_TOKEN from .env. Keep this behind one interface so local and remote are interchangeable.
- Write a .env.example with USE_REMOTE, REPLICATE_API_TOKEN, HF_HOME. Never hardcode secrets.

Features that must work:
- Prompt box, negative prompt box, width and height selects, steps, guidance, and a seed field with a "random" toggle.
- A "variation" button on any gallery item: reopens its exact settings so you can change only the lighting or background wording and re-run, keeping the seed fixed.
- Upload endpoint accepting JPG and PNG up to 20 MB, validated by content type and actual decode, then usable as the img2img source.
- Gallery grid of all past generations with prompt, seed and settings stored in SQLite.
- Compare view: pick exactly two gallery items, show them side by side at equal height with their settings diffed underneath.
- Delete an item, which removes both the row and the file.

Out of scope, do not build: inpainting, upscaling, ControlNet, user auth, multi user support, watermarking, payments, Docker.

Deliver a README with exact setup commands, the VRAM expectation, and how to flip to the remote provider. Then run the app once and confirm one text-to-image generation and one img2img generation complete end to end.
